metadata.jobDescription:
Circle - Developer Pillar Organization

Circle is a Web3 infrastructure company building the rails for the internet of money.
Beyond USDC, Circle provides APIs, SDKs, and programmable wallets for developers
building on blockchain infrastructure.

Team responsible for:
- USDC on-chain development
- L1 ARC launch
- Developer tools and integrations

Context from initial conversation with Thomas:
- Multiple openings across the Dev pillar organization
- Approach: find right person first, then align to appropriate role
- 4-5 hires made last year, 2-3 more planned this year
- Interest in AI agent economy and real-world USDC use cases

Background alignment:
- Developer relations and integrations focus
- EVM integration experience from Anchorage
- Institutional custody and staking background
- AI research interest: agent-to-agent transactions using USDC

hero.subheadline: Product Manager with 8+ years shipping Web3 developer tools and protocol integrations. From Ankr's API platform to Anchorage's L2 integrations—I help developers build on blockchain infrastructure. Now exploring how USDC becomes the economic rails for AI agents.

about.tagline: Eight years building developer tools at the intersection of Web3 and real-world utility.
bio:
I got into crypto to solve a real problem: my uncle in Spain needs to send money to family in Moldova, and the existing rails are broken. When I saw USDC kiosks appearing in remote European towns, I knew stablecoins had crossed from speculation to infrastructure. That's the Circle I want to help build—not just a stablecoin, but the developer platform that makes global value transfer as simple as an API call.
At Anchorage, I led the EVM integration team shipping 8 protocol integrations at 4× industry speed. Before that, I built Ankr's Advanced API serving 1M+ daily requests and SDK suite with 1,900+ weekly downloads. At Dapper, I improved Flow developer onboarding by 60%. The thread through my career is the same: {{accent}}make it easier for developers to build on blockchain{{/accent}}. Now I'm researching agent-to-agent transactions—AI agents that can hold wallets, transact autonomously, and use USDC as their native currency. Circle is building the infrastructure that makes this possible.
